items.name: LL-37
items.benefits: Investigational topical wound-healing evidence is mixed. A 25-person diabetic-foot-ulcer trial reported improved granulation tissue, without significant wound-area reduction. A larger 148-person venous-ulcer trial found no overall healing advantage; a favorable large-ulcer subgroup was exploratory. These findings do not establish benefit from systemic injections or treating infections.

provenance.locator: Dosing Protocol & Schedule; source timing statements

source_statements.excerpt: The only human timeline data comes from the wound trials. There, twice-weekly topical LL-37 improved healing rates over a 4-week (first-in-man) and 13-week (Phase IIb) treatment window, with the strongest effect in large, long-standing ulcers.

For injectable community use, there is no validated timeline because it has not been studied in human trials. Any promised week-by-week result should be treated as unsupported. For research planning, the practical focus is monitoring the injection site, tracking skin or inflammatory changes, and stopping
